nodes.label: Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption
nodes.rationale: Encrypt before put, decrypt on get, under a per-persistenceId subkey derived from the master key. Protects against more threats than server-side encryption alone — credential compromise, provider compromise, 'we hold the keys' audits — at the cost of CPU and key management.

nodes.label: MasterKeyRing
nodes.rationale: active is what new writes encrypt under; retired keys stay to decrypt historical blobs. Each entry's version byte travels in the body manifest so decrypt can pick the matching key — the foundation of online rotation.

nodes.label: HKDF info context binding
nodes.rationale: The subkey derives from the master key, the persistenceId as HKDF salt, and info. It is required with no default on purpose: a shared default would let two deployments holding the same master key derive byte-for-byte the same subkey, so a staging environment restored from a production dump could read production's blobs with nothing in the config saying so. info is NOT recorded on the wire, so changing it makes every existing blob undecryptable until a sweep rewrites them — pick it before the first write.

nodes.label: Body integrity (HMAC-SHA256)
nodes.rationale: Encryption is not integrity: an unencrypted body is plain JSON anyone who can write the object can edit — including the revision field the durable-state CAS is built on. The tag covers the whole framed body, manifest header included, so the compression and encryption flags are authenticated too. Its key is separate from the encryption master key because the threat is tampering, not disclosure. A snapshot is the more valuable target, since recovery folds events on top of it.

nodes.label: The tag is required, not merely checked
nodes.rationale: The bit recording 'this body has a tag' lives in the body, so whoever can rewrite the object can clear it and drop the 16 tag bytes. If an absent tag meant 'skip verification' the check would protect nobody — stripping a tag is far easier than forging one.

nodes.label: allowUntaggedBodies migration window
nodes.rationale: Bodies written before integrity was enabled carry no tag and would be refused, so the window is opened explicitly, the corpus rewritten (load + upsert per persistenceId), and the option removed again. While it is set an untagged body is accepted from anyone. Snapshots migrate on their own as keepN prunes the untagged ones.

nodes.label: Binding a body to its storage key
nodes.rationale: A tag answers 'did the key holder produce these bytes', not 'were they produced for this object', so an authentic body moved to another key used to verify there just as well — one account's object copied onto another's key came back as that account's state. HKDF salting narrowed it to one pid but still allowed replay onto another sequence number. Every write now binds the storage key into AES-GCM's AAD or, length-prefixed, into the HMAC input, with a manifest bit recording it.

nodes.label: requireContextBinding
nodes.rationale: Pre-binding bodies still decode so an old bucket keeps working — which is also the gap, because the 'bound' bit is a manifest byte, so one authentic unbound body stays a replay token for every key in the bucket until unbound bodies stop being accepted. Rewrite the corpus first or reads start failing. Also: the binding covers the whole storage key including prefix, so changing prefix breaks verification.

nodes.label: Rollback protection (durable state)
nodes.rationale: The same body at the same key, just older, is invisible to every authenticator: it was written by the legitimate writer and the revision sits inside the bytes the tag covers. ObjectStorageDurableStateStore instead remembers the highest revision seen per persistenceId and refuses to load below it. Two limits: the floor is in-process and forgotten on restart, and it fires on a legitimate delete-and-recreate from another writer — which is what withRejectRevisionRollback(false) exists for.

nodes.label: encryptionByPrefix resolver
nodes.rationale: withEncryption accepts a per-persistenceId resolver, not just a flat config, so when a tenant maps to a pid prefix each tenant gets its own key with no wrapper or custom store.

nodes.label: Integrity and master-key rotation do not compose yet
nodes.rationale: reEncryptObjectStorage supplies no integrity key, so it cannot read tagged bodies and a sweep over them fails (#739). Finish any pending key rotation before enabling integrity on a bucket.

nodes.label: Lose the key, lose the data
nodes.rationale: Master keys must be backed up — KMS backups, escrow, multiple geographic copies. Encryption without recovery is data destruction, and server-side replication copies the ciphertext but not the keyring.
